Figure 4.28: Allegra simulations at 40 ns into the current pulse of Mykonos shot 17133. The
images show the current, magnetic field across the gap, current density in the cathode, and
temperature in the cathode. The lineouts of each of the profiles shown are taken at either
the foil-edge location or the foil-middle location, as represented by Fig. 4.27, right panel.
[Simulation data courtesy of Alex Sarracino, Derek Lamppa, and Kyle Cochrane from Sandia
National Laboratories.]

comparison.limits: These are published current display comparisons, not raw waveforms or registered physical drive inputs. Literal CSV decimal cells define exact rational central knots and readout bounds. Supplied bounds are estimated publication readout envelopes; their adequacy as physical or certified source-error bounds is not established. Central PL extrema are continuous on common finite support. The separate readout diagnostic is evaluated at an explicit finite query set. Its conservative box interpretation allows only strictly order-preserving piecewise-linear vertex retiming and vertical vertex bounds; any actual-error member must satisfy those supplied bounds. Max horizontal displacement r bounds the corresponding nominal coordinate tau by |tau-q|<=r, so extrema of the lower/upper current PL on[q-r,q+r] enclose that retimed display. Whole horizontal windows must remain within central supplied support; edge queries lacking support have no readout interval. Correlated calibration and pixel errors are unknown; independent boxes provide an outer set, not a probability law. Zero inclusion does not prove simultaneous or continuous agreement. Zero exclusion is conditional display-coordinate disagreement only, and identifies neither an erroneous simulation drive nor a physical clock, normalization or trigger error. Filtering, averaging, scaling, preprocessing and more general coordinate relations remain unresolved. No offset, amplitude fit, time warp, smoothing, tail, prehistory, physical derivative or extrapolation is added. No chi-squared, statistical significance, pseudo-independent sample noise or RMS is computed. Finite-query vertical bars in figures are not interpolation of an exact continuous uncertainty envelope. No source/CR/FLASH/Quark producer is called.

comparison_completion.final_scientific_interpretation: No evaluated fully supported outer readout interval excludes zero. This is finite-query non-exclusion under supplied estimated boxes and monotone PL display retiming, not proof of agreement or shared physical clocks. Central PL differences remain explicitly nonzero; their cause is unresolved.

findings.subject: continuous central extrema
findings.reason: The difference of the two central displays is linear between consecutive members of their union of knot times. On finite shared support, its minimum, maximum and maximum absolute value occur at the support endpoints or a union knot. The code includes those endpoints and uses exact rational CSV decimal declarations.

findings.subject: outer intervals under horizontal and vertical vertex boxes
findings.reason: For retimed adjacent vertices s_i and s_(i+1), write a bracketed query q as their convex combination and use the same weight to form nominal tau from t_i and t_(i+1). The global maximum horizontal box radius r gives abs(tau-q)<=r. Vertical vertex bounds enclose the retimed value between the lower and upper nominal PL displays at tau. Taking their extrema over [q-r,q+r], at window endpoints and interior knots, therefore supplies an outer interval. Difference bounds [left_lower-right_upper,left_upper-right_lower] are conservative.

findings.subject: finite support and edge handling
findings.reason: Central interpolation rejects queries outside the original central support. Pair queries are restricted to the central support intersection. Outer intervals are omitted unless each complete horizontal window lies within that curve's central support; the reported qualified domain matches those global-radius margins. No prehistory, tail or snapshot endpoint is inserted.

findings.subject: interpretation of the finite-query outer diagnostic
findings.reason: The shifted-knot query set is not treated as a certificate of continuous-envelope extrema or joint compatibility. Summary and notes explicitly distinguish continuous central PL extrema from finite-query outer intervals. Zero inclusion means non-exclusion by the conservative outer set, and does not establish agreement or a shared admissible retiming.

findings.subject: clock and uncertainty claims
findings.reason: The code compares unshifted published coordinates and performs no offset, amplitude or time-warp optimization. Vertex retiming is a stated conditional envelope model rather than a fitted correction. Supplied readout boxes are explicitly estimated display bounds, not certified physical errors, statistical noise or confidence intervals. Unknown correlations are relaxed by an outer set; they are not estimated.
